item.title: [HSBA.L] HSBC profit underwhelms on surprise $400 million private credit loss
item.description:
STORY: HSBC on Tuesday reported an unexpected $400 million loss linked to a fraud case in Britain...

The loss shows why regulators worldwide have become more concerned about banks' exposure to the $3.5 trillion private credit industry...

highlighting the often indirect and opaque nature of the lending.

British bank HSBC lent money to a private equity firm, which in turn financed a securitisation.

That's the form of lending made notorious during the 2008 financial crisis in which smaller loans such as mortgages are packaged together and sold to investors.

HSBC's chief financial officer declined to identify the firm involved when questioned by reporters on Tuesday.

But confirmed the exposure was to "private credit-related loans".

HSBC shares have risen by more than half in the last year.

But they dropped 5% in morning trade on the news.

The emergence of wider signs of stress in private credit has driven regulators in the U.S., Britain and elsewhere to probe lenders' exposure.

HSBC - Europe's largest bank - posted pretax profit of $9.4 billion for January-March - below analyst forecasts.

In summary, we are executing our plan, delivering operational excellence to our customers, investing in grid expansion to serve Arizona’s rapid growth, and improving investment recovery to reduce regulatory lag while ensuring affordability for customers.
